scope: Historical PR 16145 ARM native startup failure, source and log comparisons, and explicitly bounded local diagnostics; no production cause or performance improvement is established.
qualifications: The failing head a53de4ffc1ac310118f57d5f722dc8968ca07e4e remains historical evidence. The failure is the unchanged 25-second initial readiness boundary, not the 90-second test ceiling or a retained-jev reader failure.

The first local invocation used layerUndici instead of the integration test's layerNodeHttp. Its HTTP result is invalid for comparison and is excluded from any startup latency or failed-CI conclusion. The original receipt and execution provenance are retained unchanged.

The single corrected local invocation used layerNodeHttp, fresh isolated application state, the pinned x64 native package and the actual production server implementation. It is not an ARM or Nix-CI reproduction, and the earlier invalid invocation may have warmed binary pages; it is not a cold-performance comparison.

Both local samplers map an unavailable children read and an empty children file to directChildCount=0. Therefore no descendant-absence conclusion may be drawn from that field or from the corrected provenance's statement about sampled direct children. This limitation supplements, rather than rewrites, the immutable originals.
Linux proc io counters include waited-for children. Scheduler counters refer to the sampled task. These are not cgroup, storage-request or exclusive native-process attribution.

The corrected run's outer-scope exit observer was interrupted. The supported cleanup observations are an ESRCH existence check for the owned PID and removal of isolated state, not an observed child exit code.
Common Nix copy warnings and overlapping independent Rust/tool prerequisites occurred in passing and failing logs. They do not establish the startup cause.

No probe deadline, outer test limit, child shutdown grace, production source, provider execution, financial authority, workflow retry, runner capacity or storage policy was changed by these observations.

limitations: No rerun or load was generated.
No storage, CPU or runner-resource correlation was collected for this failure.

findings: The failed ARM initial phase reached its unchanged25-second readiness deadline without an HTTP response; its recorded transport errors have no errno/cause detail.
The same-head AMD and accepted ARM runs eventually produced HTTP200 and wrapper-listening markers. Suppressed native child output prevents identifying its precise listen/handler/bootstrap phase.
Accepted437 ARM passed initial readiness at24,507ms,493ms below the25,000ms deadline; this is a margin observation, not justification to relax the deadline.

The same four Rust toolchain copy messages and a pre-header download-buffer warning occur in the failed ARM and both compared successful full logs. Those messages do not isolate CPU or storage as the cause.
No CPU, PSI, cgroup-throttling, I/O-latency or device-queue measurement is retained in these compared logs.
limits: Unchanged source does not prove identical runtime/cache/runner conditions.
The log header is earlier than the startup-phase clock; copy-log overlap uses the explicit header-to-initial-diagnostic interval, not a claimed exact child boot interval.
The broad diagnostic text search only establishes absent matching markers; it is not a resource measurement.
No native child stdout/stderr was available, so absence of a native listen marker is not evidence that the socket never listened.
Transport counters distinguish HTTP, cancellation and transport outcomes but do not retain underlying syscall error codes.
Passing and failed runs occurred at different times and architectures; this is not a controlled performance experiment.

qualifications: All 12 selected native runtime/packaging/test blobs match across failing a53, accepted acc and releasing 6d. Equality does not establish or dismiss the failure's cause.
The source comparison is bounded to named paths, not all repository files or runtime environments.

findings: CLI builds Global/AppProcess/Npm/Config/Updater/observability, dispatches the serve handler, and builds its isolated Global layer before the native listener.

ServerProcess.start binds the listener, attaches a dispatch handler, then constructs application services. Authenticated GET /api/info is answered during asynchronous boot with pinned-version 503; no request-triggered application initialization exists on this path.

An accepted request before dispatch installation can be unanswered; the existing 1s probe cancellation repairs that race. The new failure already exercises repeated cancellations, so this source race alone does not explain it.

Synchronous native SQLite Database construction, WAL pragma, statement.all and fresh-schema transaction lie on global bootstrap. They can block the event loop while executing; the failed CI has no child bootstrap/IO observation proving they caused its stall.
Fresh schema bootstrap is already one transaction, not one commit per migration. Legacy V1 migration is forked after services are built.

Inspected Git/AppProcess/Npm layers construct deferred methods; Updater construction reads local metadata, and PersistentPty starts a daemon only on use or inherited handoff. No pre-response git/rg lookup was demonstrated. PATH equivalence remains an environmental distinction, not a justified change.
No source-supported production correction was identified. The corrected local x64 startup passed with potentially warmed binary pages and cannot establish the ARM-CI cause.
